complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintaining an ordered structure of inserted keys allows depth derivation in O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate identifies that node depth is 1 + max(depth[pred], depth[succ]) without constructing the tree explicitly.

hints.title: Parent Relationship In Ordered Keys
hints.text: When a new key is added to the binary tree, its direct parent is always either its immediate predecessor or successor among previously inserted keys.

hints.title: Depth Formula from Neighbors
hints.text: The depth of the newly inserted node equals one plus the maximum depth between its predecessor and successor.

hints.title: Sorted Range Lookups
hints.text: Query neighboring keys in an ordered set or binary search structure to retrieve predecessor and successor depths in logarithmic time.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import bisect

class Solution:
    def maxDepthBST(self, order: list[int]) -> int:
        inserted = []
        depth = {}
        max_d = 0

        for x in order:
            idx = bisect.bisect_left(inserted, x)
            pred_d = depth[inserted[idx - 1]] if idx > 0 else 0
            succ_d = depth[inserted[idx]] if idx < len(inserted) else 0
            d = 1 + max(pred_d, succ_d)
            depth[x] = d
            if d > max_d:
                max_d = d
            inserted.insert(idx, x)

        return max_d
```
